title: CDC says a child need not finish the bottle or the plate, and food is not a prize
summary: CDC says to let the child decide how much to eat, and that food is not a good reward or punishment.
body: The CDC hunger and fullness page, dated 11 March 2026, says to let the child decide how much they want. A child does not need to finish a bottle or all of the food in the jar or on the plate. Food is not a good reward or punishment. The page says to talk with the child's doctor or nurse if a caregiver is concerned about how much or how little the child is eating. That last step is a conversation, not a diagnosis printed by the page. The advice is from a United States infant and toddler nutrition page. It is not a rule for every culture's table.

sources.title: Signs Your Child Is Hungry or Full
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: Supports the child-decides and not-a-reward sentences. Public-domain CDC page. Paraphrased.
